# Converted native argument bindings

First principles: a Go function representation conversion does not change the
caller's native runner binding. The old raw StaticCallee path lost four proved
converted parameter/capture cases; direct native baselines passed. Current
ArgumentBindings consumes the same authenticated source projector as CalleeSource
and LastFunctionArgument. The projector also lends its already-validated native
closure to Primitive's binding iterator. No public carrier, wrapper, alias,
function registry or copied graph is added.

Local positive/refusal/neutral tests exercise actual capture, missing capture and
a different caller argument. The finite nine-mode semantic partition crosses
converted named/literal/captured source and isolated call/value custody damage.
The existing malformed-tail, foreign capture, future closure, cancellation,
consumer-stop and 32/8193-width allocation checks exercise the changed producer.
Native fault checks delete the closure loan and break lexical/original operand
custody. All attempts and source-bound native output remain retained.

Old authored fault fixtures are refreshed only where this cut made a previously
applicable fixture stale. Earlier, already-inapplicable historical fixtures are
preserved with their original executable evidence; they are not counted as
current causal proof. This slice's current faults execute the current source.

Benchmarks and fuzz run serially for three seconds after tests and tools. Native
compiler construction remains a separately owned whole-unit operation. These are
development facts, not independent acceptance or a claim about arbitrary-depth
runtime or fabricated generic-instance canonical identity.
